conflicts.issue: Premature Application of Draft Southeast Durham Plan Policies & Comprehensive Plan Engagement
conflicts.summary: During the Comprehensive Plan update, Mark-Anthony Middleton raised strong concern that City Council colleagues were already citing the un-adopted draft Southeast Focus Area Plan against rezoning applications (such as Courtyards at Doc Nichols) before JCCPC review or adoption, alongside debate over how Planning engages local builders and residents.
conflicts.side_a_position: Do not apply un-adopted draft Southeast Durham Focus Area Plan maps to defeat current zoning cases, and provide more direct staff engagement channels for residents.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton noted developers and Council members lacked official clarity because the Southeast Focus Area Plan remained an un-adopted draft with open policy questions.
Middleton urged making Planning staff more directly accessible to citizens intimidated by technical mapping jargon.
conflicts.side_b_position: Use the draft place-type framework iteratively across fall community workshops and engage local infill practitioners before formal adoption.
side_b_arguments: Staff and Chair Jacobs clarified the Southeast Focus Area work was intended as an iterative testing lab rather than an adopted plan.
Javiera Caballero and Pierce Freelon emphasized incorporating local small-scale builders, architects, and multi-channel neighborhood workshops into refining the place types.
conflicts.resolution: Informational / Guidance provided to Planning staff ahead of fall workshops and November follow-up

conflicts.meeting_title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - April 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
conflicts.issue: Land Use Engagement Initiative Scope, Early Public Comment Risks, and Developer Engagement Training
conflicts.summary: During review of the Land Use Engagement Initiative and Social Pinpoint tool, Council members diverged over whether staff should train developers on engagement and how early public commenting should be framed relative to statutory authority.
conflicts.side_a_position: Question spending limited Planning staff time training developers and warn that unstructured early commenting can mislead residents about what local boards can legally regulate.
side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece objected at 01:24:48 to using scarce public staff hours to train private developers on engagement instead of equipping neighborhood residents to organize and putting raw resident input directly before elected officials.

Javiera Caballero argued at 01:21:47 that while interactive maps boost transparency, early open commenting without clear legal guardrails risks raising expectations on issues outside City/County jurisdiction such as state NCDOT roads.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support shifting public input earlier into the pre-submission design phase to make land-use engagement more egalitarian and set clear expectations for applicants.
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton praised the initiative at 01:40:09 for elevating early neighborhood feedback before project plans lock in, while urging the portal to surface developer proffers and historic neighborhood context.
Planning Director Sara Young clarified at 01:35:29 that the department's primary client is the public and that developer guidance raises engagement expectations rather than advocating for applicants.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote required on the engagement demo; staff noted Council feedback for implementation and JCCPC unanimously recommended the overall FY2021-22 Work Program at 02:20:12.

conflicts.meeting_title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) Feb 3, 2021 (Live Stream)
conflicts.issue: Developer Criticism of the Durham Planning Commission's Review Role and Continuance Practices
conflicts.summary: During the Planning Commission's 2020 annual report, Mark-Anthony Middleton voiced external developer complaints accusing the Planning Commission of acting like an 'activist Supreme Court,' prompting pushback from Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Planning Commission Chair Brian Buzby.
conflicts.side_a_position: Address developer perception that Planning Commission overreaches beyond technical UDO/Comprehensive Plan advisory review.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton asked Chair Brian Buzby directly how to respond to developers who complain the Planning Commission has drifted into acting as an 'activist Supreme Court' rather than an advisory zoning body.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defend Planning Commission independence, diverse representation, and community-engagement rigor before Council votes.
side_b_arguments: Planning Commission Chair Brian Buzby explained the Commission strictly issues recommendations rather than final votes and noted continuances often stem from applicants submitting revised plans late or skipping neighborhood meetings (citing Fawcett Avenue).
Charlie Reece defended the Planning Commission's statutory advisory role and public hearing scrutiny as critical input for elected officials.
Javiera Caballero praised the Planning Commission's diversity and equity focus as essential to representing underrepresented residents.
conflicts.resolution: Informational exchange with no vote; committee members moved on to the Comprehensive Plan objectives briefing.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - December 1, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs with City Council representatives Mark-Anthony Middleton, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero present alongside Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Planning Commissioner Austin Amendolia, the Joint City-County Planning Committee voted 6-0 to excuse Commissioner Brenda Howerton and approve the October 6, 2021 minutes. Planning staff presented the Comprehensive Plan Draft Place Type Map and engagement rollout, highlighting Urban Growth Boundary pullbacks near Falls Lake and 15-minute community concepts, and walked through Omnibus 17 UDO Text Amendments. Members directed staff to explore full parking-minimum elimination for existing building change-of-use and height/density incentives for solar and green buildings, while also reviewing Expanding Housing Choice Q3 2021 permit trends (194 permits since October 2019), Census data delays, and scheduling joint annual commission reports.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Brenda Howerton, and Approval of October 6 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs introduced new committee clerk Terry Elliott and conducted roll call with Vice Chair Mark-Anthony Middleton, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, and Planning Commissioner Austin Amendolia present. The committee passed two 6-0 roll-call votes to grant Commissioner Brenda Howerton an excused absence and approve the October 6, 2021 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Update — Community Engagement and Draft Place Type Map
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller and Scott Whiteman presented the draft Place Type Map featuring 20 place types, Urban Growth Boundary pullbacks in Northeast Durham and the Falls Lake watershed, Future Growth Areas, and 15-minute communities. Members praised the GIS feedback portal, raised questions on Arrowhead-area boundaries and how staff reports will apply place types in future zoning cases, and urged proactive public outreach.

agenda_items.title: Omnibus 17 UDO Text Amendments Review and Parking/Solar Policy Direction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock outlined Omnibus 17 UDO revisions transferring floodplain administration to the Planning Director, addressing RDU avigation easements, R&D districts, small/flag lots, cemeteries, stub-out payment-in-lieu options, bike lanes behind bus stops, design-district S2 transitions, and expanding change-of-use parking exemptions from 20% to 50%. Committee members gave thumbs-up direction to explore eliminating change-of-use minimum parking altogether and creating solar/green-building density or height bonuses.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choice Q3 2021 Update, Census Delay Briefing, and Annual Commission Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman reported 194 Expanding Housing Choice permits since October 2019 (including small-lot single-family homes, duplexes, and ADUs), updated tear-down statistics, and new tax-office home-price trend charts showing single-family sales rising from ~$130k in 1997 to ~$360k. Staff also briefed members on 2020 Census data release delays affecting annual reporting and discussed scheduling annual joint board/commission presentations with Sarah Young.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) Augst 4, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) convened on August 4, 2021 (indexed under date 2021-08-05), chaired by BOCC Commissioner Wendy Jacobs alongside JCCPC Vice Chair Mark-Anthony Middleton and Council Member Javiera Caballero. After recognizing longtime Planning clerk Susan Cole on her upcoming retirement, the committee approved its June 2, 2021 minutes by unanimous roll-call vote (including Aye from Middleton). Planning staff presented the Comprehensive Plan phase-two working group structure and draft Southeast Durham Focus Area recommendations, prompting discussion with Caballero and Middleton on 15-minute walkable neighborhoods, density versus rural-lot flexibility, voluntary proffers under the City's affordable housing charter provision, and expedited review incentives. Staff also delivered the tri-annual Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) metrics update—reporting 150 EHC-enabled permits applied for, primarily lot splits and small-lot options—before adjourning without further votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Recognition of Clerk Susan Cole, and Approval of June 2, 2021 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the JCCPC meeting and Planning Director Sara Young announced that longtime committee clerk Susan Cole was on leave caring for her father and retiring after more than 20 years with Planning and over 30 years in Durham local government. The committee then approved the June 2, 2021 minutes unanimously on motion by Planning Commissioner Brian Busby and second by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Policy Working Groups and Draft Southeast Durham Focus Area Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Lisa Miller, Kayla Seibel, and Sara Young) outlined cross-departmental policy working groups and presented draft place types and recommendations for the Southeast Durham Focus Area. Council Member Javiera Caballero, Vice Chair Mark-Anthony Middleton, and BOCC members discussed how to make '15-minute neighborhoods' enforceable when proffers are voluntary, balancing housing density and transit access against rural/large-lot flexibility, using development agreements and expedited approvals under the City's affordable housing charter provision, and learning from the 2005 comprehensive plan.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) Tri-Annual Metrics Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staffer Scott Whiteman reported that 150 EHC-enabled permits had been applied for to date, heavily concentrated in lot splits and small-lot options, while legally binding affordable units had risen by roughly 1,000 as naturally occurring affordable units fell by roughly 1,000. Whiteman also explained that City-County GIS could supply land-value-per-square-foot and new-unit-price metrics for the next report, whereas Census racial/income data lagged prior to EHC's 2019 adoption.

votes.item_title: Approval of June 2, 2021 JCCPC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint committee roll call (BOCC Chair Wendy Jacobs, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, Planning Commissioner Brian Busby, and City Council Vice Chair Mark-Anthony Middleton; Council Member Javiera Caballero also participated in the meeting). Only City roster member explicitly heard on the roll-call excerpt is Mark-Anthony Middleton.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the June 2, 2021 JCCPC minutes was moved by Planning Commissioner Brian Busby and seconded by BOCC Commissioner Nimasheena Burns.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) June 2, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) met virtually on June 2, 2021—with BOCC Commissioner Wendy Jacobs presiding alongside City Council members Javiera Caballero and Pierce Freelon, while Mark-Anthony Middleton and Charlie Reece were excused. The committee approved three unanimous 6-0 procedural motions: excusing Middleton's absence, excusing Reece's absence, and approving the April 7, 2021 minutes. Planning staff outlined the upcoming 2022 Comprehensive Plan adoption schedule, policy-development framework, Southeast Durham and Braggtown focus areas, and equity report card metrics. Planner Michael Stock also briefed the committee on North Carolina legislative proposals affecting local zoning authority (including downzoning limits, Board of Adjustment remote-hearing fixes, and tree-ordinance preemption) and on UDO Article 3 text amendments codifying street closings/renamings, annexations, multi-era development-plan modifications, expanded renter notice, and color-coded rezoning signs.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absences (Mark-Anthony Middleton and Charlie Reece), and April 7, 2021 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Opening the virtual JCCPC meeting with Planning Director Sara Young attending during vacation, the committee conducted roll call and passed three 6-0 motions: excusing City Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton (moved by Pierce Freelon, seconded by Javiera Caballero), excusing City Council Member Charlie Reece (moved by Planning Commissioner Brian Busby, seconded by Freelon), and approving the April 7, 2021 minutes (moved by Freelon, seconded by Caballero).

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Scope, Schedule, Focus Areas (Southeast Durham and Braggtown), and Equity Report Card
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reviewed the adoption schedule for the Community Goals and Objectives (June 15 joint public hearing, June 21 City Council vote, June 28 BOCC vote) and detailed phase-two policy work targeting completion in late 2022. Staff explained why Southeast Durham (US-70 to NC-98/county line) was selected for urgent rezoning guidance and Braggtown (along Roxboro Road) was selected for equitable neighborhood partnership, alongside an equity report card tracking race, income, and environmental justice data points.

agenda_items.title: North Carolina State Legislative Update on Planning and Zoning Bills
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock reviewed General Assembly bills affecting local planning, including housing-type preemption and downzoning limits, remote Board of Adjustment hearing fixes eliminating unanimous-consent stalls, tree-ordinance restrictions opposed across jurisdictions, mandatory school permissions across zoning districts, native landscaping requirements, and five-mile airport rezoning notice rules.

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Article 3 Text Amendments Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented proposed UDO Article 3 amendments incorporating street-closing, street-renaming (codifying 911 naming rules), and annexation procedures into the UDO, clarifying contiguous development plans across rights-of-way, codifying rules across three historical eras of development plans, removing Planning Director discretion on obsolete proffers, and improving public notice to renters/duplex addresses and color-coded roadside signage.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - April 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: The April 7, 2021 Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) meeting, chaired by Durham County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs with seated City Council members Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Mark-Anthony Middleton attending, took two unanimous 6-0 committee votes: approving the corrected February 3, 2021 minutes and recommending adoption of the FY2021-22 Planning Department Work Program. The committee received 2020 annual reports from the Appearance Commission and the Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) Commission (which requested two new open-space/trails planners and flagged Neighborhood Matching Grant cap limits) and heard updates on the Comprehensive Plan's revised Community Goals & Objectives and Southeast Focus Area outreach. Members engaged in a pointed policy debate over the Land Use Engagement Initiative, with Charlie Reece and Javiera Caballero warning against spending staff time training developers or creating misleading early comment loops, while Mark-Anthony Middleton praised the initiative's earlier, more egalitarian timing. Planning staff also reported on Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) monitoring challenges—noting proprietary market data would be needed to track land values and naturally occurring affordable housing—and pending NC House Bill 401.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Approval of February 3, 2021 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual JCCPC meeting with City Council members Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Mark-Anthony Middleton, County Commissioner Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby present (County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns joined later). Members corrected two clerical items in the February 3 minutes (an officer election vote tally corrected from 6-1 to 6-0 and Commissioner Howerton's name spelling) and approved the minutes unanimously 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Appearance Commission 2020 Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Appearance Commission representative Kayla Seibel presented the 2020 annual report detailing design review work, downtown and corridor aesthetic guidelines, and collaboration with Planning staff during virtual operations. Committee members thanked the volunteer board and asked brief clarifying questions.

agenda_items.title: Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) Commission 2020 Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DOST Commission representative Carl Kolosna presented the 2020 annual report, formally requesting one new City Urban Open Space planner and one new County trails planner to handle surging land-development case reviews. DOST also flagged that the $77,000 Neighborhood Matching Grants cap forced several applicants to be turned away.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Revised Community Goals & Objectives and Southeast Focus Area Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Brooke and Lisa updated JCCPC on revised Community Goals and Objectives and Southeast Focus Area engagement led alongside outreach ambassadors Ethel Simonetti, Vanessa Evans, and Constance Wright. Staff outlined the timeline toward an April 27 Planning Commission public hearing and June 15 joint adoption.

agenda_items.title: Land Use Engagement Initiative and Social Pinpoint Interactive Map Demo
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Alexandra Cahill and Chris Peterson presented the Land Use Engagement Initiative and demonstrated an interactive Social Pinpoint development case map intended to surface neighborhood comments earlier in the review timeline. Charlie Reece objected to devoting limited Planning staff capacity to training developers, Javiera Caballero cautioned against setting unrealistic expectations on state-controlled roads or non-binding comments, and Mark-Anthony Middleton supported weighting early community feedback more equitably alongside proffer visibility.

agenda_items.title: Expanding Housing Choice (EHC) Metrics Update and FY2021-22 Planning Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented EHC monitoring metrics, reporting that staff currently lack proprietary real estate datasets needed to track land-value changes, naturally occurring affordable housing (NOAH), or racial income shifts without an external data RFP, and briefed members on state House Bill 401 ('missing middle' housing). Following discussion, JCCPC voted unanimously 6-0 to recommend approval of the FY2021-22 Planning Department Work Program.

votes.item_title: Approve Corrected Minutes of February 3, 2021 JCCPC Meeting
votes.notes: Motion moved by County Commissioner Brenda Howerton and seconded by Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby; full committee passed 6-0 with Chair Wendy Jacobs, Brenda Howerton, Brian Buzby, and the three seated City Council members voting Aye (Nimasheena Burns joined later).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved February 3, 2021 minutes with two technical corrections changing a reported officer vote from 6-1 to 6-0 and correcting Commissioner Brenda Howerton's name spelling.

votes.notes: Full JCCPC committee voted 6-0 with Chair Wendy Jacobs, County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby, and the three seated City Council members voting Aye (Brenda Howerton departed prior to the final vote).
votes.discussion_detail: Recommended joint approval of the FY2021-22 City-County Planning Department Work Program incorporating Comprehensive Plan, Engagement Initiative, and EHC monitoring tasks.

side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece objected at 01:24:48 to using scarce public staff hours to train private developers on engagement instead of equipping neighborhood residents to organize and putting raw resident input directly before elected officials.

Javiera Caballero argued at 01:21:47 that while interactive maps boost transparency, early open commenting without clear legal guardrails risks raising expectations on issues outside City/County jurisdiction such as state NCDOT roads.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support shifting public input earlier into the pre-submission design phase to make land-use engagement more egalitarian and set clear expectations for applicants.
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton praised the initiative at 01:40:09 for elevating early neighborhood feedback before project plans lock in, while urging the portal to surface developer proffers and historic neighborhood context.
Planning Director Sara Young clarified at 01:35:29 that the department's primary client is the public and that developer guidance raises engagement expectations rather than advocating for applicants.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote required on the engagement demo; staff noted Council feedback for implementation and JCCPC unanimously recommended the overall FY2021-22 Work Program at 02:20:12.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) Feb 3, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 3, 2021 Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) meeting, outgoing Chair Charlie Reece presided over the opening roll call (joined by City Council members Javiera Caballero and Mark-Anthony Middleton, County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby; Commissioner Nimasheena Burns joined at 00:30:44 and Council Member DeDreana Freeman observed briefly at 01:17:22). The committee unanimously voted 6-0 to elect Wendy Jacobs as 2021 Chair and Mark-Anthony Middleton as Vice Chair, and voted 6-0 to approve the December 2, 2020 minutes. Following annual reports from the Board of Adjustment, Historic Preservation Commission, and Planning Commission, Mark-Anthony Middleton pressed Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby on developer complaints that the Planning Commission acts like an 'activist Supreme Court,' prompting Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Buzby to defend neighborhood engagement and advisory review. Members gave thumbs-up consensus endorsing 33 draft Comprehensive Plan objectives (including Southeast Durham focus work), reviewed 16 proposed omnibus UDO text amendments (TC2100001), and agreed to shift Expanding Housing Choices reporting from every two months to every four months.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Election of 2021 Officers, and Approval of December 2, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Chair Charlie Reece opened the virtual JCCPC meeting at 9:30 AM with three City Council representatives (Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton), County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda Howerton, and Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby present. The committee voted 6-0 to elect Wendy Jacobs as Chair and Mark-Anthony Middleton as Vice Chair—turning the gavel over to Jacobs at 00:03:56—and voted 6-0 to approve the December 2, 2020 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Board of Adjustment (~45 cases), Historic Preservation Commission (22 COAs), and Planning Commission (55 cases)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and commission leaders reviewed 2020 annual reports for the Board of Adjustment (Jessica Dockery and Chair Jacob Rogers), Historic Preservation Commission (Grace Smith and Katie Hamilton), and Planning Commission (Grace Smith and Chair Brian Buzby, 55 rezoning/plan cases). Mark-Anthony Middleton raised developer complaints that the Planning Commission acts as an 'activist Supreme Court,' sparking debate in which Buzby, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero defended public engagement, diversity, and advisory review.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan 33 Draft Objectives and Southeast Durham Focus Area
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Lisa Miller, Kayla Seibel, and Ami Mejia presented 33 draft Comprehensive Plan objectives color-coded by land-use nexus (strong, moderate, weak) alongside Southeast Durham focus-area public input (with County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns arriving at 00:30:44 and Council Member DeDreana Freeman observing at 01:17:22). After discussion of school-capacity coordination, infrastructure, and rural equity, committee members gave unanimous thumbs-up consensus approving the draft objectives while retaining cross-referenced moderate/weak goals.

agenda_items.title: Omnibus 16 UDO Text Amendments (TC2100001) and Expanding Housing Choices Reporting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock briefed the committee on TC2100001 Omnibus 16 UDO amendments, including flexible virtual/in-person procedures, dropping newspaper notices for quasi-judicial hearings where not required, replacing boarding houses with co-living, expanding shelters/food pantries/meal centers, height limits in RSM/OICG/RC/S2, stream-buffer variances, and stub-street notices. Members also agreed at 01:53:16 to move Expanding Housing Choices progress reporting from every two months to every four months before adjourning at 11:25 AM.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus to initiate text amendments and adjust EHC cadence (No formal vote)

votes.item_title: Election of 2021 JCCPC Officers (Wendy Jacobs as Chair, Mark-Anthony Middleton as Vice Chair)
votes.notes: Full JCCPC vote was 6-0 including County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Brenda Howerton and Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby (County Commissioner Nimasheena Burns joined later at 00:30:44). Per roster scoping, ayes lists the seated City Council members participating on the committee.
votes.discussion_detail: Joint City-County Planning Committee voted unanimously 6-0 to elect County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as Chair and City Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton as Vice Chair for 2021.

votes.notes: Full JCCPC roll-call vote was 6-0 including Commissioners Jacobs and Howerton and Planning Commissioner Buzby; ayes lists the seated City Council committee members.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion by County Commissioner Brenda Howerton and second by Planning Commissioner Brian Buzby to approve the December 2, 2020 JCCPC minutes.

disagreements.meeting_title: Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) Feb 3, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Developer Criticism of the Durham Planning Commission's Review Role and Continuance Practices
disagreements.summary: During the Planning Commission's 2020 annual report, Mark-Anthony Middleton voiced external developer complaints accusing the Planning Commission of acting like an 'activist Supreme Court,' prompting pushback from Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, and Planning Commission Chair Brian Buzby.
disagreements.side_a_position: Address developer perception that Planning Commission overreaches beyond technical UDO/Comprehensive Plan advisory review.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton asked Chair Brian Buzby directly how to respond to developers who complain the Planning Commission has drifted into acting as an 'activist Supreme Court' rather than an advisory zoning body.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend Planning Commission independence, diverse representation, and community-engagement rigor before Council votes.
side_b_arguments: Planning Commission Chair Brian Buzby explained the Commission strictly issues recommendations rather than final votes and noted continuances often stem from applicants submitting revised plans late or skipping neighborhood meetings (citing Fawcett Avenue).
Charlie Reece defended the Planning Commission's statutory advisory role and public hearing scrutiny as critical input for elected officials.
Javiera Caballero praised the Planning Commission's diversity and equity focus as essential to representing underrepresented residents.
disagreements.resolution: Informational exchange with no vote; committee members moved on to the Comprehensive Plan objectives briefing.
